self-management education for cancer patients has been shown to have a positive effect in the management of symptoms and quality of life.

self-management education programs for patients with cancer are associated with improved outcomes for fatigue, pain, anxiety, depression and quality of life.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an evidence based, theory informed, self-management education intervention for people with cancer, which is delivered by health care professionals and/or peer supporters.
the development of a self-management support program for patients with cancer.
the development and implementation of a model of self-management support for patients with cancer and their families.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is insufficient evidence to determine the core components and elements of self-management that should be included in interventions to support effective self-management for patients with cancer.

there is a need to develop a consensus regarding core elements and components of self-management support to ensure that patients are able to manage their disease, treatment-related side effects and long-term effects effectively.
self-management interventions for patients with a cancer diagnosis are effective in improving quality of life and reducing symptoms such as fatigue, pain, anxiety and depression.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there is a need for a more rigorous approach to evaluating self-management education interventions.
the current literature does not support any one combination of elements or core components of self-management interventions.

self-management education for cancer is a promising approach, however, there is a need for further research to determine which components of self-management interventions are effective in supporting self-management in cancer.

the core elements and the fundamental elements need further refinement to determine which elements of self-management interventions are effective in the context of cancer.
the field of cancer self-management is in need of a more systematic and rigorous approach to defining core components and essential elements of self-management support.
we need to better understand what is meant by the core components of self-management support and how they are operationalized in practice.
